newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian privatisation minister Kokh resigns.
newsitem.headline: Russian privatisation minister Kokh resigns.

text.p: Russian privatisation minister Alfred Kokh has resigned and will be replaced by another ally of economic policy chief Anatoly Chubais, a spokesman for President Boris Yeltsin said on Wednesday.

Kokh, who resigned as Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the State Property Committee, will be replaced in both posts by Maxim Boiko, currently deputy head of Yeltsin's administration. Previously Boiko headed the Russian Privatisation Centre.
Both Kokh, 36, and Boiko are close to Chubais, who is one of two first deputy prime minister's in Yeltsin's government.
Kokh has presided over a particularly stormy phase of Russian privatisation and was singled out for criticism recently by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

The biggest sell-off yet, the sale last month of one quarter of telecommunications company Svyazinvest, prompted an unprecedented outcry in media controlled by businessmen linked to the losing consortium.

The sale this month of a controlling 38 percent stake in Russia's biggest mining company, Norilsk Nickel, also proved controversial, with Chernomyrdin trying to have the sale stopped until the last minute. Kokh also halted the controversial privatisation of Russia's biggest insurer, Rosgosstrakh, in June.
